case_name: Keith Thaete, Steve King, Lance Thaete v. St. Luke's Magic Valley Center, Michael R. Fry, D.O

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction from nonservice
issues.why: The court must decide whether failure to serve the notice of appeal deprives the appellate court of jurisdiction or can be cured.

issues.label: Timeliness of notice of appeal
issues.why: The court must confirm the notice of appeal was filed within the time allowed from a final, appealable judgment.

issues.label: Finality of appealed orders
issues.why: The court must determine whether the challenged rulings merged into a final judgment or are independently appealable.

issues.label: Preservation of issues for appeal
issues.why: The court must decide whether arguments were properly raised below (e.g., in opposition or reconsideration) to be reviewed.

issues.label: Standard of review selection
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (abuse of discretion for striking/exclusion; de novo for summary judgment; statutory review for foundation).

issues.label: Lunneborg abuse-of-discretion analysis
issues.why: For motions to strike and evidentiary sanctions, the court must apply the four-part Lunneborg framework to each decision.

issues.label: Authority to strike late filings
issues.why: The court must determine the trial court’s power under rules/scheduling orders to strike untimely summary-judgment materials.

issues.label: Good cause/excusable neglect for lateness
issues.why: The court must consider whether late expert declarations/responses should be allowed based on good cause, excusable neglect, or fairness.

issues.label: Impact of court-ordered response deadline
issues.why: The court must interpret how the August 22 deadline interacted with prior disclosure deadlines and the hearing continuance.

issues.label: Proper scope of rebuttal evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether “rebuttal” expert declarations may address elements of plaintiffs’ case-in-chief on summary judgment.

issues.label: New opinions vs permissible supplementation
issues.why: The court must determine whether the late declarations were improper new standard-of-care opinions or permissible clarifications.

issues.label: Prejudice to defendants from late opinions
issues.why: The court must assess whether allowing late expert opinions would prejudice defendants (e.g., no time to depose/obtain counterproof).

issues.label: Availability of lesser sanctions
issues.why: Before striking/excluding, the court should consider whether lesser measures (continuance, re-opening discovery, costs) were appropriate.

issues.label: Enforcement of amended scheduling orders
issues.why: The court must decide whether expert-disclosure deadlines were clear, complied with, and properly enforced.

issues.label: Treatment of supplemental witness disclosure
issues.why: The court must decide whether identifying Nurse Tripp as a supplemental witness complied with disclosure rules and scheduling orders.

issues.label: Untimeliness of Nurse Tripp disclosure
issues.why: The court must determine if Tripp’s disclosure violated the amended order and whether exclusion was warranted.

issues.label: Required content of expert disclosures
issues.why: The court must decide whether disclosures contained the required opinions, bases, and subject matter to support trial/summary judgment use.

issues.label: Nurse Chisum breach-opinion disclosure
issues.why: The court must determine whether Chisum was actually disclosed to opine on breach and whether the record supports that.

issues.label: Effect of counsel representations
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether counsel’s statements that Chisum was unwilling to testify justify exclusion or estoppel.

issues.label: Ability to rely on non-testifying expert
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs can defeat summary judgment with an expert who is unwilling/unavailable to testify.

issues.label: Reconsideration standards and scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether the reconsideration motion properly presented new evidence/arguments and the correct standard was applied.

issues.label: Record on summary judgment
issues.why: The court must identify what materials were properly in the summary-judgment record after striking and how they should be construed.

issues.label: IRCP 56 burden-shifting compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure defendants met their initial burden and that plaintiffs produced admissible evidence creating a genuine dispute.

issues.label: Admissibility vs weight distinction
issues.why: The court must separate foundational admissibility rulings from credibility/weight determinations reserved for the factfinder.

issues.label: Necessity of expert testimony
issues.why: The court must decide whether expert testimony is required for standard of care/breach/causation or whether any exception applies.

issues.label: Common-knowledge exception applicability
issues.why: The court must consider whether prescribing a contraindicated drug without medication reconciliation is within lay comprehension.

issues.label: Idaho Code 6-1012 locality rule
issues.why: The court must determine whether the expert established knowledge of the applicable community standard of care or similar community.

issues.label: Idaho Code 6-1013 foundation requirements
issues.why: The court must decide whether the expert’s foundation shows actual knowledge through training, practice, study, or consultation.

issues.label: Definition of relevant ‘community’
issues.why: The court must identify the proper community standard (Twin Falls/hospital setting) and whether a similar community was shown.

issues.label: Same specialty requirement
issues.why: The court must determine whether the proffered physician expert is in the same specialty as Dr. Fry for standard-of-care testimony.

issues.label: Board certification relevance
issues.why: The court must assess whether shared board certification supports familiarity with the standard of care under Idaho’s statutes.

issues.label: Foundation from expert’s preparation
issues.why: The court must decide whether review of records, policies, depositions, or consultation sufficiently established actual knowledge.

issues.label: Reliance on Dr. Fry deposition precision
issues.why: The court must determine whether perceived imprecision in Dr. Fry’s deposition is a proper basis to find the expert lacks foundation.

issues.label: Hospital standard-of-care expert foundation
issues.why: The court must decide whether Dr. Dodson (or another expert) had foundation to opine on St. Luke’s policies/practices and nursing duties.

issues.label: Nursing standard of care proof
issues.why: The court must determine whether nursing experts properly established nursing standard of care, breach, and causation for hospital liability.

issues.label: Vicarious liability vs direct liability
issues.why: The court must clarify whether claims against St. Luke’s are based on employee negligence, policy failures, credentialing, or direct negligence.

issues.label: Dr. Fry employment/agency status
issues.why: The court must decide whether Dr. Fry was an agent/employee of St. Luke’s for vicarious liability purposes (if asserted).

issues.label: Medication reconciliation duty scope
issues.why: The court must determine the standard of care regarding obtaining/recording home meds when family provides prescription bottles.

issues.label: Knowledge of Nardil prescription
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence creates a genuine dispute that Dr. Fry knew or should have known about Nardil.

issues.label: Contraindication awareness duty
issues.why: The court must consider the duty to check interactions/contraindications before prescribing Paxil in the hospital setting.

issues.label: Breach by prescribing Paxil
issues.why: The court must decide whether prescribing Paxil under these facts constitutes a deviation from the applicable standard of care.

issues.label: Breach by nursing administration
issues.why: The court must determine whether nursing staff breached duties by administering Paxil despite contraindications or incomplete med history.

issues.label: Causation medical probability standard
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiffs produced admissible expert evidence that the breach more probably than not caused death.

issues.label: Proximate cause and intervening causes
issues.why: The court must consider whether any intervening medical conditions, treatment decisions, or patient factors break causation.

issues.label: Wrongful death and survival standing
issues.why: The court must confirm proper parties and statutory authority to bring claims given Sherry’s death and Keith’s capacity.

issues.label: Damages elements proof requirements
issues.why: The court must identify what damages are recoverable (economic/non-economic) and whether expert proof is required for any element.

issues.label: Comparative fault considerations
issues.why: The court must consider any asserted comparative negligence or fault allocation issues (e.g., information provided by family/patient history).

issues.label: Negligence per se viability
issues.why: The court must decide whether negligence per se is available under the Medical Malpractice Act and what statute/rule would supply the duty.

issues.label: Reckless conduct/punitive threshold
issues.why: The court must determine whether pleadings/evidence support reckless conduct or punitive damages standards, if pursued.

issues.label: Effect of discovery rulings on fairness
issues.why: The court must assess whether limitations on policy discovery affected plaintiffs’ ability to establish standard of care or respond to summary judgment.

issues.label: Use of hospital policies as evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether internal policies are admissible/usable to establish standard of care or notice and how they interact with locality rule.

issues.label: Disclosure of policies timing impact
issues.why: The court must consider whether late-produced policies justify later supplementation or rebuttal opinions by plaintiffs’ experts.

issues.label: Expert opinion on ultimate issues
issues.why: The court must ensure expert testimony fits within admissible opinion boundaries and is not impermissible legal conclusion.

issues.label: Hearsay and affidavit form compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure expert declarations comply with affidavit requirements (personal knowledge, admissible facts, proper attachments).

issues.label: Authentication of exhibits
issues.why: The court must determine whether medical records, policies, and deposition excerpts were properly authenticated for summary judgment.

issues.label: Duty of hospital to supervise
issues.why: The court must decide whether a hospital has a duty to ensure safe prescribing/med reconciliation by internists and nursing staff.

issues.label: Corporate negligence theory applicability
issues.why: The court must consider whether Idaho recognizes/permits corporate negligence claims against hospitals on these facts and required proof.

issues.label: Attorney fees entitlement basis
issues.why: The court must decide whether any statute/rule authorizes fees (e.g., frivolous appeal/defense, contractual, or discretionary provisions).

issues.label: Prevailing party determination
issues.why: The court must decide who is the prevailing party for purposes of costs and fees at each stage.

issues.label: Costs on appeal and below
issues.why: The court must resolve taxable costs and procedures depending on outcome and any rule-based entitlements.

issues.label: Appropriate appellate remedy
issues.why: If error is found, the court must decide whether to reverse and remand for trial, reopen discovery, or limit issues on remand.
